messages:
Maya: heads-up: after landing AWQ-int8 sparse profile on the canary pool, we see a formatting/hallucination spike on the code-structure benchmark :eyes:
bench-bot: automated run 3344556677: code-struct suite results:
```
fp16 baseline: exact_match=92.12%, json_schema_valid=98.7%
awq-int8-sparse: exact_match=86.45%, json_schema_valid=92.3%
delta: exact_match -5.67pp, schema_valid -6.4pp
```
Maya: that's a pretty big delta for that workload, and the failure mode is structured output fields being reordered / numeric fields invented
Sam: can you paste a failing example?
Maya: sure, here's one (trimmed):
```
prompt: "Extract invoice table to JSON"
fp16 -> {"items": [{"qty": 3, "price": 19.99}, {"qty": 1, "price": 5.00}], "total": 64.97}
awq-int8 -> {"items": [{"price": 19.99, "qty": 3}, {"qty": 1, "price": 5.00}], "total": "sixty-four dollars"}
```
Maya: note the total becomes free-form text and sometimes missing decimals; also keys shuffled in some runs
Eli: interesting — key order shouldn't matter for JSON schema, but our downstream expects canonical order for diff-based checks. Does this repro deterministically or intermittently?
Maya: intermittent (~30% of runs on the canary), not deterministic per-se.
Zara: did we change tokenization or seeding between profiles? AWQ introduced a different packing for sparse kernels last patch.
Sam: I ran a quick bisect between commit a1b2c3(fp16 baseline) -> d4e5f6(awq merge). Early results point to the awq packing + shared-KV sharding tweak.
bench-bot: intervention note: canary config used: pool=canary-sparse, batch_shape=[1,1], seq_bucket=[128,512], kv_shard=2, fallback=gptq-int8
Eli: kv_shard change is suspicious — sharding + sparse kernels can alter memory layout and numerical reorderings. Also check prefix caching differences (cache alignment can change rounding).
Maya: I repro'd locally with `--kv-shard 2 --quant-profile awq-int8-sparse` and got same weird total formatting. Dumped logits around the numeric token boundary and saw a softmax nudge.
Sam: can you paste the logits diff? small sample ok
Maya: pasted to gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/awq-logit-diff (contains a tiny diff showing probability mass shift at tokens [".", "0", "9"])
Zara: quick experiment: if you force `kv_shard=1` on the awq profile, does it improve?
Maya: yes — kv_shard=1 drops the JSON_schema_valid delta to -1.2pp and exact_match to -1.0pp. So sharding is likely contributing.
Eli: still, behavior changed only under AWQ-int8-sparse. fp16 with kv_shard=2 was fine historically, right?
Sam: correct — fp16+kv_shard=2 passes. So it's the combination of awq quant kernels + sharding.
Maya: action items I propose:
- rollback canary to gptq-int8 for now (keep host capacity)
- open a kernel/kv-shard repro ticket and attach failing prompt + logit diff
- run targeted microbench: run same prompt with varying seq_len and shard counts to map boundary
- consider a temporary policy: prefer kv_shard=1 for awq-int8-sparse model variants until resolved
Zara: +1. Also add a synthetic suite of numeric-boundary cases to our canary so we catch this earlier.
Eli: I'll take the repro ticket and try a narrow quant-calibration sweep (per-channel scale vs per-tensor) to see if quantization scale interacts with shard alignment.
Sam: if calibration fixes it then we can keep shard=2. If not, we should add a runtime fallback rule in routing: if model_variant contains awq-int8-sparse and route.kv_shard>1 then fallback to gptq-int8.
Maya: I'll schedule a short canary rollback and update the rollout notes. Anyone object?
Eli: no objections. tagging @oncall-ml in case we need infra help for kernel repro.
Sam: logging note: capture full wasm kernel config + env (MKL/CUDA flags) — differences in rounding across drivers have bitten us before.
bench-bot: created ticket RDW-ML-5123: "AWQ-int8-sparse + kv_shard=2 -> structured-output hallucination spike" (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RDW-ML-5123)
Maya: thanks — I'll add the failing-case collection and assign test matrix to the ticket.
Zara: one more ask: can we tag models in the model-catalog with a note about shard-sensitivity? makes it clearer for infra when configuring dedicated pools.
Maya: added note in the ticket. ok rolling back canary now. :thumbsup:
Sam: thanks everyone, good catch.
